name: How do contractors prevent roof leaks where the new metal addition joins the old building?
description: Contractors use custom transition flashing, closure strips, and engineered water drainage paths tucked under existing panels to prevent leaks at tie-in points.

mainEntity.name: How do contractors prevent roof leaks where the new metal addition joins the old building?

acceptedAnswer.text: Proper weatherproofing relies on engineered transition flashings, rubber closure strips, and high-grade sealants specifically placed where the addition meets the existing roof and walls. Water management is critical at roof tie-ins: your contractor must account for drainage slope and ensure the new roof does not dump stormwater runoff onto the existing structure. Depending on the design, counter-flashing must be tucked under the original metal panels, and expanded valleys or gutters must be sized to handle heavy downpours without backing up under seams.
